relevance_note: Cohort of 31 Japanese Alexander disease probands with per-patient GFAP mutation, sex, ages and initial symptom in Table 1 ("Clinical information is presented in Table 1").
method_note: Read the whole paper including the converted supplement. Table 1 (31 patients, one row each) was transcribed by a Python script in my scratch directory that parses the Markdown rows; I checked every row's mutation, sex, ages, initial symptom and Ref cell against the table by eye. Labels: Table 1 has a bare-number "No." column, so patients are "Table 1 #<n>", except the two the text names: "patient 12" (Results) and "Patient 13" (Supplementary materials S3/S4, "(Patient 13, E362G)"). The ^a marks on Nos. 2, 4, 10, 11 are footnotes, not part of the label. Scope: 42 patients were genetically diagnosed but only the 31 included probands are described individually; the other 11 (4 non-consenting, 5 cerebral type, 2 non-proband relatives among the 33) have no individual detail and get no rows. cohort_size_as_stated = 31 (included probands). Ref cells copied verbatim into source_reference_in_review (multi-line cells such as "^7,\n10,\n11" kept as printed; numbers refer to the paper's reference list). Disease subtype: the converted Table 1 has a "Bulbospinal type" section row before No. 13, so Nos. 13-31 get "Bulbospinal type" (span = section row + patient row); the header for the first section (Nos. 1-12) is missing from the conversion, so only Nos. 2, 4, 10, 11 (footnote a: reclassified as intermediate form) get "intermediate form"; Nos. 1, 3, 5-9 and patient 12 get "AxD" (group wording), although the text's counts (12 intermediate, 19 bulbospinal) imply they are intermediate form. Zygosity "heterozygous" from the Methods group statement ("Forty-two Japanese AxD patients ... with heterozygous GFAP mutations"), which includes all 31. Ethnicity from "the patients were all Japanese". is_proband from "31 probands were included". Variants are protein short forms only (e.g. R79H); recorded in variant_original_string and protein_hgvs_as_stated; no cDNA or transcript printed; variant type not stated per variant, so not reported. Pathogenicity left not reported: Table S7 and Fig. 3 give only in-silico tool predictions (PROVEAN Neutral/Deleterious etc.), not the authors' classification. Phenotypes: the only per-patient feature is the initial symptom (Table 1); recorded as observed with severity_or_detail "initial symptom"; onset of the feature left null (not stated separately). "NA" initial symptoms (Nos. 7, 24) and NA onset (patient 12) treated as not reported. Checklist mapping: Dysarthria -> dysarthria or dysphonia; Dysphagia -> dysphagia; Limb weakness -> limb weakness; Dementia -> cognitive decline; Incontinence -> autonomic dysfunction (bladder or bowel dysfunction). "Weakness" (No. 15, limb not stated), "Limb clumsiness", "Gait disturbance", "Blurred vision" and "Mental retardation" were not mapped to checklist items. No MRI item was marked: subtype definitions and diagnostic criteria (e.g. bulbospinal type = medulla/cervical cord abnormality) are criteria, not per-person findings. Table 2 and Tables S1-S4 give group genotype counts for modifier SNPs (other genes, group-level only, not attributed to persons): no rows. No contradictions found within the paper; Table 1 places No. 13 (onset 12 years) in the bulbospinal section, consistent with the text (younger-onset 92% intermediate = 12/13).
